claims.statement: Dalaketnon are evil engkanto, environmental spirits often in human form, an elf-like race with pointed ears in Philippine mythology; in Visayan culture they were thought beautiful like pre-Hispanic nobles and monarchs, men light-skinned and dark-haired, women bronze-brown.
claims.statement_id: Dalaketnon adalah engkanto jahat, roh lingkungan yang sering tampil dalam wujud manusia, bangsa mirip peri bertelinga runcing dalam mitologi Filipina; dalam budaya Visayas mereka diyakini rupawan seperti bangsawan dan raja Filipina prakolonial, laki-laki berkulit terang berambut gelap dan perempuan berkulit cokelat perunggu.
claims.quote: Dalaketnon are evil engkanto, or mythological environmental spirits that often appear in human form. Dalaketnons are a race of elf-like creatures in Philippine mythology with pointed, leaf-shaped ears. In Visayan culture, they were believed to be handsome and beautiful beings resembling nobles and monarchs of pre-Hispanic Philippines.

claims.statement: The name dalaketnon comes from these spirits living in dalakit trees (balete or dakit), meaning 'from the dalakit tree'.
claims.statement_id: Nama dalaketnon berasal dari kepercayaan bahwa roh ini tinggal di pohon dalakit (balete atau dakit), dan berarti 'dari pohon dalakit'.
claims.quote: The name dalaketnon comes from the fact that these spirits are said to reside in Dalakit trees (also known as Balete or Dakit), with their name meaning "from the Dalakit (or Dakit) tree."

claims.statement: In folklore these beings abduct people to their world and feast them; victims must eat black rice, which enchants them so they cannot escape.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, makhluk ini menculik orang ke dunianya dan menjamu mereka; korban dipaksa memakan nasi hitam yang membuat mereka terpesona dan tak bisa melarikan diri.
claims.quote: According to folklore, these creatures abduct people and take them to their own world, where they prepare feasts for their captives. The victims are forced to eat Black Rice, which is believed to place them under the creatures’ enchantment and prevent them from escaping.

claims.statement: The elderly believed dalaketnon could turn humans into their kind with magical black rice; they were enemies of benevolent engkanto, royal rulers of the evil ones, linked with the tiyanak, aswang, manananggal and tiktik.
claims.statement_id: Orang tua dulu percaya dalaketnon dapat mengubah manusia menjadi seperti mereka dengan nasi hitam ajaib; mereka musuh bebuyutan engkanto yang baik, keturunan bangsawan dan penguasa engkanto jahat, serta dikaitkan dengan tiyanak, aswang, manananggal, dan tiktik.
claims.quote: According to folklore, the elderly believed that Dalaketnons possessed the ability to transform ordinary humans into beings like themselves, using magical black rice for this purpose. They were also thought to be mortal enemies of the benevolent engkanto.

claims.statement: Kong koi or Phi Kong Koi (ผีกองกอย) is a Lao and Thai jungle ghost, often one-legged, hopping and shouting koi; some say it has a fly-like tube mouth, others that it looks like a monkey or langur; most agree it is ugly and cannot climb trees.
claims.statement_id: Kong koi atau Phi Kong Koi (ผีกองกอย) adalah hantu hutan Laos dan Thailand, sering digambarkan berkaki satu, melompat sambil berteriak koi; sebagian percaya mulutnya berupa tabung seperti lalat, sebagian menggambarkannya mirip monyet atau lutung; kebanyakan sepakat ia buruk rupa dan tak bisa memanjat pohon.
claims.quote: is a Lao and Thai jungle ghost. Their appearance is not easily characterized, but often described as a phantom with one leg. They move by hopping with one leg and shout, "Koi, koi, koi". Some people believe it has a fly-like tube mouth. Others describe it as looking like monkey or langur. Most agree this ghost is ugly and cannot climb trees

claims.statement: Phi Kong Koi is believed to suck blood from sleeping travellers' toes; travellers should keep their feet together or crossed when sleeping.
claims.statement_id: Phi Kong Koi dipercaya mengisap darah dari jari kaki pengembara yang tidur di hutan; pengembara sebaiknya merapatkan atau menyilangkan kaki saat tidur.
claims.quote: It is believed that the Phi Kong Koi will suck blood from the toes of the sleeping traveler in the jungle; Travelers should keep the feet together or cross their feet when sleeping to protect themselves.

claims.statement: Some call it Phi Pong or Phi Pong Kang ('mineral lick ghost') and Phi Teen Diao ('one-footed ghost').
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menyebutnya Phi Pong atau Phi Pong Kang ('hantu tempat jilatan garam') dan Phi Teen Diao ('hantu berkaki satu').
claims.quote: some people use the term Phi Pong (ผีโป่ง) or Phi Pong Kang (ผีโป่งค่าง; 'mineral lick ghost') and Phi Teen Diao (ผีตีนเดียว; 'one-footed ghost').

claims.statement: The Tai Dam of Nong Sung, Mukdahan, believe Phi Kong Koi is a tiny long-haired woman with backwards feet who speaks the opposite of reality; fish or valuables on forest paths must not be taken, being hers.
claims.statement_id: Orang Tai Dam di Nong Sung, Mukdahan, percaya Phi Kong Koi adalah perempuan sangat kecil berambut panjang dengan kaki terbalik yang berbicara kebalikan dari kenyataan; ikan atau barang berharga di jalan hutan tidak boleh diambil karena miliknya.
claims.quote: In the faith of Tai Dam in Nong Sung district, Mukdahan province, they believe that Phi Kong Koi is a long-haired, very small (childlike) woman with backwards feet. They speak the opposite of reality. It is also believed that fish or valuables found along forest paths should not be taken, as they belong to Phi Kong Koi

claims.statement: Luang Pu Waen Suciṇṇo told of meeting many Phi Kong Koi in the forests of Khammouane, Laos, shaped like children of 13–14, thin with bulging bellies, dark brown skin and small crossbows.
claims.statement_id: Luang Pu Waen Suciṇṇo menceritakan bertemu banyak Phi Kong Koi di hutan Khammouane, Laos, yang berwujud seperti anak 13–14 tahun, kurus berperut buncit, berkulit cokelat gelap, dan bersenjata busur kecil.
claims.quote: He described the Phi Kong Koi as being shaped like children of about 13–14 years old. They were thin with a bulging belly, dark brown skin, dark hair, and a chubby nose. They were armed with small crossbows or arrows

claims.statement: The nawarupa (နဝရူပ, also Nawa Rupa; Pali navarūpa, 'nine forms'), also called byala, is a chimeric creature of Burmese and Rakhine (Arakanese) mythology.
claims.statement_id: Nawarupa (နဝရူပ, juga Nawa Rupa; Pali navarūpa, 'sembilan wujud'), juga disebut Byala, adalah makhluk campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar dan Rakhine (Arakan).
claims.quote: Nawarupa (Burmese: နဝရူပ, also spelt Nawa Rupa; Pali: navarūpa, Sanskrit: नवरूप, lit. 'nine forms'), also known as Byala (Rakhine: ဗျာလ, ဗျာလ္လ), is a chimeric creature found in Burmese and Rakhine (Arakanese) mythology.

claims.statement: The beast is made of 9 animals: an elephant's head, deer's eyes, rhinoceros horns, a parrot's tongue and wings, a lion's body and legs, and a peafowl's tail.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini tersusun dari 9 hewan: kepala gajah, mata rusa, tanduk badak, lidah dan sayap burung nuri, tubuh dan kaki singa, serta ekor merak.
claims.quote: The beast is made of 9 animals, possessing the head of an elephant, the eyes of a deer, the horns of a rhinoceros, the tongue and wings of a parrot, the body and legs of a lion, and the tail of a peafowl.

claims.statement: In the Konbaung dynasty, the nawarupa decorated a ceremonial royal barge.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa dinasti Konbaung, nawarupa menghiasi salah satu perahu upacara kerajaan.
claims.quote: In the Konbaung dynasty, the nawarupa decorated one of the ceremonial royal barges.

claims.statement: The nuno sa punso ('old man of the mound'), or nuno ('old man', 'ancestor'), is a dwarf-like nature spirit of Philippine mythology believed to live in an anthill or termite mound.
claims.statement_id: Nuno sa punso ('kakek dari gundukan'), atau nuno ('kakek', 'leluhur'), adalah roh alam mirip kurcaci dalam mitologi Filipina yang dipercaya tinggal di sarang semut atau gundukan rayap.
claims.quote: A nuno sa punso ("old man of the mound"), or simply nuno ("old man" or "grandparent" "ancestor"), is a dwarf-like nature spirit in Philippine mythology. It is believed to live in an anthill or termite mound, hence its name

claims.statement: The nuno are ancestral spirits; before felling a tree or breaking new ground, people ask their permission to avoid the misfortune of angering them.
claims.statement_id: Nuno adalah roh leluhur; sebelum menebang pohon atau membuka tanah baru, orang meminta izin kepadanya agar terhindar dari malapetaka karena membuatnya marah.
claims.quote: The nuno are the spirits of the ancestors. When a tree is to be felled, or a piece of virgin ground broken, or on many other occasions, permission is asked of the nuno, in order to avoid the misfortune that would come from angering it.

claims.statement: The nuno is a tiny old man, unlike the playful dwende who appears to children; the nuno is easily angered and punishes those who damage his mound, e.g. swelling the foot that kicked it; he also lives under large rocks, trees, riverbanks, caves or gardens.
claims.statement_id: Nuno digambarkan sebagai kakek mungil, berbeda dengan dwende yang suka bermain dengan anak-anak; nuno mudah marah dan membalas orang yang merusak gundukannya, misalnya membuat kaki yang menendangnya bengkak; ia juga tinggal di bawah batu besar, pohon, tepi sungai, gua, atau kebun.
claims.quote: The dwende is a playful hobgoblin who shows himself to children, while the nuno is a goblin easily angered that will do harm to those who damage or disturb his mound, and will seek retribution, for example by causing the foot of someone who kicked his mound to become swollen.

claims.statement: Nunos can curse trespassers with swelling or pain and excessive back hair, usually by spitting on them.
claims.statement_id: Nuno dapat mengutuk penyusup dengan bengkak atau nyeri di bagian tubuh dan tumbuhnya bulu berlebihan di punggung, biasanya dengan meludahinya.
claims.quote: Nunos have the ability to curse trespassers. ... Swelling or pain on any part of the body ... Excessive hair growth on the back

claims.statement: It is commonly believed in the Philippines that illness modern medicine cannot cure may be a nuno's curse; the victim goes to an albularyo, a traditional healer, who performs pagtatawas divination with alum or wax melted into water.
claims.statement_id: Di Filipina umum dipercaya bahwa penyakit yang tak tersembuhkan obat modern mungkin akibat kutukan nuno; korban dibawa ke albularyo, tabib tradisional, yang melakukan ramalan pagtatawas dengan tawas atau lilin yang dilelehkan ke air.
claims.quote: It is a common belief in the Philippines that if modern medicine is unable to cure a particular illness, the ailment may be due to a nuno's curse. The victim is brought to an albularyo, a Philippine practitioner of traditional medicine. The albularyo will perform a type of divination known as pagtatawas.

claims.statement: To be cured, the victim's family may offer fruit, food, drink or an object to the nuno; if still ill, they may need to ask its forgiveness in person.
claims.statement_id: Untuk sembuh, keluarga korban dapat diminta memberi persembahan buah, makanan, minuman, atau benda kepada nuno; bila masih sakit, perlu meminta maaf langsung kepadanya.
claims.quote: In order to be cured, the victim's family may be asked to provide an offering to the nuno such as fruits or other food, drink, or a material object. If the victim is still sick after the offering, it may be necessary to personally ask the nuno's forgiveness

claims.statement: Elders in the Philippine provinces taught people always to excuse themselves (tabi tabi po) when passing an earth mound.
claims.statement_id: Orang tua di provinsi Filipina mengajarkan untuk selalu meminta permisi (tabi tabi po) setiap kali melewati gundukan tanah.
claims.quote: our elders instructed us always to excuse ourselves (thus the term “tabi tabi po” became a common phrase in our country) whenever we are passing by this soil formation

claims.statement: Maximo Ramos described dwarves or duwende as 'spirit of the fields', 'spirit of the hills' and 'people of the ground'.
claims.statement_id: Maximo Ramos menggambarkan kurcaci atau duwende sebagai 'roh ladang', 'roh bukit', dan 'orang tanah'.
claims.quote: The late Dr. Maximo Ramos, one of the early scholars who created a compendium of lower mythological creatures of the Philippines, describe Dwarves or Duwende as a “spirit of the fields”, “spirit of the hills” and “people of the ground.”

claims.statement: In Philippine mythology, the sirena is a legendary water creature with a woman's head and torso and a fish's tail from the waist down; she is an engkanto, the Filipino counterpart of the English mermaid.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, sirena adalah makhluk air legendaris berkepala dan bertubuh atas perempuan dengan ekor ikan dari pinggang ke bawah; sirena adalah engkanto, padanan Filipina bagi putri duyung Inggris.
claims.quote: In Philippine mythology, the Sirena is a mythological aquatic legendary creature with the head and torso of a human female from waist down and the tail of a fish. The Sirena is an Engkanto –' the Filipino counterpart of English mermaids.

claims.statement: The sirena is one of the bantay tubig (water guardians), with the siyokoy, kataw and ugkoy; the male version is the sireno, and sirenas are sometimes paired with siyokoy.
claims.statement_id: Sirena termasuk bantay tubig (penjaga perairan), bersama siyokoy, kataw, dan ugkoy; versi laki-lakinya disebut sireno, dan sirena kadang dipasangkan dengan siyokoy.
claims.quote: Engkantos are classified as one of the Bantay Tubig, (guardian of a body of water) a Filipino term for mythical guardians of the water. In addition to the Sirena, other examples of Bantay Tubig are Siyokoy, Kataw, and Ugkoy. The male version of a Sirena is called a Sireno. Sometimes, Sirena are paired with Siyokoy.

claims.statement: The sirena's beautiful voice lures and hypnotizes men, especially fishermen; she sings to sailors until they neglect their work, walk off decks or are shipwrecked.
claims.statement_id: Sirena bersuara indah yang memikat dan menghipnotis laki-laki, terutama nelayan; ia bernyanyi kepada pelaut hingga mereka lalai, terjatuh dari geladak, atau kapalnya karam.
claims.quote: The Sirena has a beautiful and enchanting voice that can attract and hypnotize males, especially fishermen. Sirena sing to sailors and enchant them, distracting them from their work and causing them to walk off ship decks or cause shipwrecks.

claims.statement: Some traditions say the sirena carries victims under the sea as sacrifices to water deities; dugongs, sea turtles and dolphins usually accompany her.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian tradisi menyebut sirena membawa korbannya ke bawah laut dan mempersembahkannya kepada dewa-dewa air; duyung, penyu, dan lumba-lumba biasanya menyertainya.
claims.quote: Some folk traditions claim that the Sirena carry their victims under the sea, sacrificing them to water deities.

claims.statement: Many Pangasinan myths tell of sirenas drowning fishermen and warriors who worship Apo Laki.
claims.statement_id: Banyak mitos Pangasinan menceritakan sirena yang menenggelamkan nelayan dan prajurit pemuja Apo Laki.
claims.quote: Many Pangasinan myths describe Sirena who drown fishermen and warriors who worship Apo laki.

claims.statement: According to the Aswang Project writer using the 160 volumes of the Beyer Ethnographic Series, sirena tales appear mainly in the Ilokano volumes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis di Aswang Project yang memakai 160 jilid Beyer Ethnographic Series, cerita sirena terutama ditemukan dalam jilid-jilid Ilokano.
claims.quote: Using the 160 volumes of the Beyer Ethnographic Series, I was amazed that the maiden of the waters was predominantly unique to the Ilokano volumes.

claims.statement: The word sirena is Spanish and has no Ilokano equivalent.
claims.statement_id: Kata sirena berasal dari bahasa Spanyol dan tidak punya padanan dalam bahasa Ilokano.
claims.quote: besides the word sirena is a Spanish word and has no Ilokano equivalent.

claims.statement: Marina was a 2004 fantasy series about a mermaid starring Claudine Barretto; a popular mermaid character in the Philippines is Dyesebel.
claims.statement_id: Marina adalah serial fantasi tentang putri duyung yang tayang pada 2004 dengan Claudine Barretto; tokoh putri duyung populer di Filipina adalah Dyesebel.
claims.quote: Marina was a fantasy series that featured a mermaid. It aired from February 23, 2004, to November 12, 2004, featuring Claudine Barretto.
